conflicts: Hook: the Handi Quilter user manual v3.3 (library-hosted copy) says 'Rotary, Horizontal axis', while our earlier spec read 'rotary vertical hook'; the spec now follows the manual.
Voltage: the manual v3.3 gives 105 to 120 VAC for the US and Canada and 100 to 250 VAC for the rest of the world, while our earlier spec said 90 to 264 VAC; the spec now follows the manual.
Motor: the manual confirms a brushless DC motor with tie-off and 300 W peak; the earlier voltage range in the motor line did not match either manual line and has been replaced.
Speed: the manual v3.3 and the dealer-hosted v3.1 copy both give 1500 spm maximum, while the Rocky Mountain Sewing dealer page says up to 1,800 spm; the page uses the manual figure.
Stitch regulation: the manual lists TruStitch as an optional accessory, while the Rocky Mountain Sewing dealer page says TruStitch is included with its package; check the quote line by line.

Throat: the maker prints 'Throat Dimensions 8.25 x 16 in' and calls it a '16-inch sit-down longarm' without saying needle to body; 16 in is the maker's wording, not a measured needle-to-body figure, and in our tiering a 16 in head sits in the mid-arm band.

Status: 'discontinued' appears on a dealer page (Rocky Mountain Sewing); Handi Quilter carries no machine page, only a parts tag archive, and a maker support article refers to the 'secondary used-machine market'.

Price: the $6,495 dealer-level figure equals the Handi Quilter list price shown for the Moxie ST, and the maker publishes no price for the Sweet Sixteen itself, so treat it as an unconfirmed dealer figure and read it as a band, not a quote.
Table: the manual gives no base table size or height range; 36 x 30 in and 26 to 42 in come from dealer copy, and dealers disagree on the range (26 to 42 in against 27 to 40 in).
Weight and size: the maker publishes no machine weight and no head dimensions; the 66.14 lb figure on the maker's lift table page is packaging for that accessory only.

ownerThemes.theme: Owners of the sit down machine say they chose it because a frame longarm strains their back and they prefer moving fabric rather than the machine; several report no service needed after dealer setup.
Prewound bobbins are blamed for tension trouble, and shop technicians agree they often do not work well on this machine; owners say learning to adjust tension yourself takes practice.

A long term owner blog calls it a joy to use but warns that large quilts around 60 by 80 in create real drag and gravity problems on a sit down table, and that owners unwilling to adjust for battings and threads will be unhappy.
A Missouri Star forum owner six months in reports it works great and is easy to use; another notes the stitch counter helps with billing for a small quilting business.

editorial.verdict: A discontinued 16 in sit-down quilter with a table and optional regulation, for a buyer who wants more throat than a domestic without a frame.
editorial.whoFor: A quilter who wants more reach than a domestic machine without giving a room to a frame, and who is happy to adjust tension and move fabric by hand on a table.
editorial.skipIf: You want stitch regulation included, you quilt king size tops often (owners report the weight of heavy quilts on the table), or you want a model Handi Quilter still lists as a machine.

faqs.q: Is the Handi Quilter Sweet Sixteen discontinued?
faqs.a: A dealer page (Rocky Mountain Sewing) says so. Handi Quilter's own wording, in a support article, is that the machine is on the secondary used-machine market, and its site carries no machine page for it, only parts and accessories. The maker never uses the word discontinued for it in the pages we read [verify].

faqs.q: What replaced the Handi Quilter Sweet Sixteen?
faqs.a: Handi Quilter staff comments name the Moxie ST and Amara ST as the stationary machines still offered, and the maker does not call either a direct replacement. handiquilter.com lists the Moxie ST at $6,495.00, with an 18 in throat, 2,100 spm and built-in stitch regulation on a 38 x 38 in InSight table. These are maker figures for the Moxie ST, not for the Sweet Sixteen [verify].

faqs.q: How much does a Handi Quilter Sweet Sixteen cost?
faqs.a: Handi Quilter publishes no price for the Sweet Sixteen because it has no current machine page. The last figure we saw was a dealer listing of $6,495 (Fig Leaf Quilting, 2026-09-29), which is unconfirmed and is the same number as the Moxie ST maker price. Handi Quilter lists the Lift Table for the Sweet Sixteen at $2,645.00. Used prices are not in our evidence [verify].

faqs.q: What do owners say about the Handi Quilter Sweet Sixteen?
faqs.a: Owners who are happy with it point to the sit-down format: several say moving the fabric by hand does not bother them, and one loves the InSight table with its built-in regulator. Recurring complaints include heavier quilts being hard to support on the table, tension that takes time to settle and one report of timing knocked out by very heavy seams. The read covers 13 Reddit threads and 1 retailer page from 2012 to 2026, and Reddit leans toward people asking for help, so problems are over-represented. Sewing Machines Plus shows 4.76 from 17 reviews, which is seller-collected.

faqs.q: Does the Handi Quilter Sweet Sixteen have a stitch regulator?
faqs.a: Not built in. The manual lists TruStitch as an optional accessory, and Handi Quilter sells a lift table with built-in InSight regulation for compatible machines on firmware 3.18 or higher. One dealer says TruStitch is included with its package, which differs from the manual [verify]. One owner says they prefer the InSight table's built-in regulator over a magnetic puck regulator.

faqs.q: How big is the throat on the Handi Quilter Sweet Sixteen?
faqs.a: The manual prints throat dimensions of 8.25 x 16 in (245 x 610 mm) and the cover calls it a 16-inch sit-down longarm; the maker does not say needle to body. In our tiering a 16 in head sits in the mid-arm band, so treat 'longarm' as the maker's wording. The manual does not label which figure is height; dealer copy says 8 inches of vertical space [verify].

faqs.q: How fast does the Handi Quilter Sweet Sixteen sew?
faqs.a: The manual lists a maximum of 1500 spm, in both the v3.3 and the v3.1 copies, with a My Speed range of 5 % to 100 %. One dealer page says up to 1,800 spm, which the manual does not support, so we use the manual figure.

faqs.q: Can you put a Handi Quilter Sweet Sixteen on a frame?
faqs.a: Handi Quilter's manual describes a sit-down machine with its own height-adjustable folding table, and the pages we read give no frame-mounting instructions. One owner on Reddit says they mounted theirs on a Grace Q-Zone frame and like it most there. That is an owner report, not a maker statement [verify].

faqs.q: What needle and bobbin does the Handi Quilter Sweet Sixteen use?
faqs.a: The manual lists needle system 134 (135 x 7) in sizes 12/80 to 20/125 and an M class aluminum bobbin with a type MF bobbin case.
